newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end down on profit taking, bankers meet.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end down on profit taking, bankers meet.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower on Friday as institutional funds locked in gains made in recent sessions ahead of the weekend, and as they await the outcome of the central bankers' meeting in Shanghai.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 4.63 points lower, 0.44 percent, at 1,041.26. The small-capitalised Second Board index shed 2.44 points, 0.44 percent, at 550.29.
"There has been profit taking today. I don't think anyone is too surprised by that," said Ooi Soon Beng, head of research at Inter-Pacific Securities.

Analysts said fund managers were awaiting the outcome of a meeting among the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) central bankers' in Shanghai to see if it would have any impact on the region's currencies or interest rates.
Telekom succumbed to profit taking, shedding 20 cents to 10.60 ringgit. The stock has a 10 percent weighting on the Composite Index.
YTL Power and Tenaga were the subject of continued institutional bargain hunting from Thursday, gaining 30 cents and 20 cents respectively.
"YTL Power is already under-rated at these prices. I have confidence in the company," said a dealer at a large local brokerage house.
Ekran, the developer of the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam in Sarawak state on Borneo island, fell five cents to 5.15 ringgit.
The company said on Thursday its differences over the project with chief contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri, remained inspite of a five-hour meeting to resolve the dispute.
Volume stood at 255 million shares valued at 1,779 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 426 to 214.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot July contract dipped 8.7 points to 1,040.1 with 1,014 lots traded. August futures lost 7.0 points to 1,041.0 with 294 lots traded.
